findings.title: Requirements for submitted programs are undocumented (public type, one main, empty args)
findings.quote: `--input` (`-i`) takes a source file, not a directory
findings.problem: No page states the preconditions a teaching program must meet. A single file or undelimited stdin input must contain exactly one public top-level type, and each file needs exactly one recognized main. The traced main always receives an empty `args` array, and no option passes program arguments. JDK 25 compact source files fail. Valid Java programs that instructors commonly use, such as a non-public `class Main` or programs that read `args[0]`, fail or behave differently. Readers cannot learn the rule before hitting it.

evidence.detail: For undelimited input (`filePaths.isEmpty()`), the code calls SourceNames.requirePublicBinaryName (SourceNames.java:57-68), which throws unless there is exactly one public top-level type.
findMain throws "must have exactly one main method" unless there is exactly one candidate.
main is invoked with no arguments or with `new String[0]`.

evidence.detail: Exit 1: "Java source code must have exactly one public top-level type declaration. Found 0 such declarations on lines []." The same class in a `// --- Main.java ---` bundle exits 0.

findings.fix: Add a "Program requirements" section to tracing.md, linked from the CLI trace-defaults table and from troubleshooting. Cover four points. Each file needs exactly one recognized main (static or instance; no parameters or String[]). `args` is always empty, so move argument-driven input to `--stdin`. Compact source files are not supported.

Valid Java programs that instructors commonly use, such as a non-public `class Main` or programs that read `args[0]`, fail or behave differently. Readers cannot learn the rule before hitting it.
findings.original_fix: Add a "Program requirements" section to tracing.md, linked from the CLI trace-defaults table and from troubleshooting. Cover four points. An undelimited file needs exactly one public top-level type; otherwise use a delimited bundle. findings.original_problem: The Java reference first says the Java request defaults to finite instructor limits, then says only that the batch protocol "preserves existing defaults". BatchTracer jobs use the NDJSON caller profile instead. Omitted `limits` are unlimited, and so is every field left out of a partial limits object. This differs from TraceLimits.builder(), which starts from instructor defaults. An embedder moving from Tracer.trace to BatchTracer for throughput, or porting TraceLimits.builder().timeoutMillis(5000).build() to {"limits":{"timeoutMillis":5000}}, silently gets jobs with no snapshot, output, heap, or byte budgets.
findings.original_fix: Replace the sentence with an explicit statement. BatchTracer jobs follow batch.md defaults, not TraceRequest defaults: omitted `limits`, and omitted fields inside it, are 0 (unlimited), and inspection defaults to TRUSTED. findings.original_problem: The Java reference covers only successful processing. batch.md:71-75 describes an oversized record only as "a CLI diagnostic and exit code 1". For Java callers, processStream throws IOException on an oversized record, an input read failure, or a writer failure. When it throws, already-admitted jobs keep running and write their responses to the caller's Writer afterwards. close() then waits up to 30 s for them before interrupting. An embedder who catches the exception and immediately writes, closes, or reuses the writer, or assumes no more output will arrive, gets unexpected late responses or a blocking close. Nothing tells them to correlate by id and treat the set as incomplete.
findings.original_fix: Add a 'Failures' paragraph to the BatchTracer section. List what makes processStream throw IOException (input read failure, writer failure, a record over 16,777,216 UTF-16 code units). State that admitted jobs may still finish and write to the caller's writer after the throw, and that close() waits up to 30 s for them. Advise keeping the writer open until close() returns and treating responses as an incomplete id-correlated set. Mention the Java behaviour next to batch.md:71-75.

findings.title: CLI exit-status table says 1 means trace generation failed; envelope guest failures also exit 1 with a trace
findings.quote: | `1` | Environment preflight or trace generation failed. | Read stderr. With an envelope, also inspect `status`, `phase`, and `diagnostics` if an envelope was produced. |
findings.problem: The exit-status contract is stated twice, and the two copies disagree. BOUNDED_TRACING.md:151-153 says that with `trace --result-envelope`, 1 means a failed job. cli.md says 1 means preflight or trace generation failed. In envelope mode, a guest uncaught exception or a guest System.exit(nonzero) gives status `failed` and exit 1, but trace generation succeeded and `trace` holds the captured snapshots. Stderr is also empty in that case, so the table's first action, "Read stderr", turns up nothing. An integrator automating on this table would treat exit 1 as "no trace" and could discard valid trace data. Row 3 has a smaller problem: it says "A tracing limit" caused the stop, but exit 3 is returned for every `stopped` status, including stops that are not budgets (unsupported_virtual_thread, value_nesting_limit, inline_value_cycle).

evidence.detail: runBounded prints the envelope and then calls exitHandler.accept(result.status().equals("stopped") ? 3 : 1) for any result that is not complete.
Status is "failed" when the stop reason ends in error or is guest_exception or guest_exit. Every other stop reason, budget or not, gives "stopped".

evidence.ref: java -jar target/code-tracer.jar trace -i Boom.java --format modern --result-envelope  (Boom.main prints 'before' then throws IllegalStateException)
evidence.detail: Exit 1 with empty stderr. The envelope has status failed, stopReason guest_exception, phase trace, complete false, and trace is non-null. The same program without --result-envelope exits 0 and prints trace JSON.
"With `trace --result-envelope`, exit codes are 0 for completed jobs, 1 for failed jobs, 2 for invalid CLI configuration, and 3 for controlled stops." This copy matches the implementation.

evidence.ref: java -jar target/code-tracer.jar trace -i Main.java --result-envelope   (Main.main prints 1, then throws IllegalStateException at line 5)
evidence.detail: exit=1, stderr empty; {"status":"failed","stopReason":"guest_exception","phase":"trace","complete":false,"diagnostics":["java.lang.IllegalStateException"]}; trace is an object with 1 snapshot, counters.snapshotsRetained=1, stdout "1\n"

evidence.ref: java -jar target/code-tracer.jar trace -i Exit.java --result-envelope   (main calls System.exit(4))
evidence.detail: exit=1, stderr empty; {"status":"failed","stopReason":"guest_exit","phase":"trace","diagnostics":["Guest process exited with code 4"],"counters":{"guestExitCode":4,...}}
'exit codes are 0 for completed jobs, 1 for failed jobs, 2 for invalid CLI configuration, and 3 for controlled stops', which is worded differently from the cli.md row.
exit=1, stdout 0 bytes; stderr: 'code-tracer: JDK environment check failed: JAVA_HOME does not select an executable java: ...'
exit=1, stdout 0 bytes; stderr: 'java.lang.RuntimeException: Failed to read stdin file: .../nope.txt at cs1302.tracer.internal.App$Trace.resolveGuestStdin(App.java:322)'
resolveGuestStdin throws RuntimeException. The catch at App.java:346 handles only IllegalArgumentException (exit 2), so this escapes to Picocli's default handler (exit 1, no envelope).
'Preflight runs before command work and can prevent an envelope from being produced.' The exit table there lists 1 as 'Environment preflight or trace generation failed'.

findings.fix: Rewrite rows 1 and 3 to split ordinary and envelope modes. Row 1, ordinary mode: preflight or trace-generation failure, no JSON. Row 1, envelope mode: the envelope `status` is `failed`, including `guest_exception` and `guest_exit`, where `trace` can still hold captured snapshots, so inspect the envelope before stderr. Row 3: any `stopped` status, budget or not. Keep one normative copy of the exit-status table (the cli.md table is the most findable) and replace the prose at BOUNDED_TRACING.md:151-159 with a link to it, so the two copies cannot drift again.

findings.original_problem: The exit-status contract is stated twice, and the two copies disagree. BOUNDED_TRACING.md:151-153 says that with `trace --result-envelope`, 1 means a failed job. cli.md says 1 means preflight or trace generation failed. In envelope mode, a guest uncaught exception or a guest System.exit(nonzero) gives status `failed` and exit 1, but trace generation succeeded and `trace` holds the captured snapshots. Stderr is also empty in that case, so the table's first action, "Read stderr", turns up nothing. An integrator automating on this table would treat exit 1 as "no trace" and could discard valid trace data. Row 3 has a smaller problem: it says "A tracing limit" caused the stop, but exit 3 is returned for every `stopped` status, including stops that are not budgets (unsupported_virtual_thread, value_nesting_limit, inline_value_cycle).
findings.original_fix: Rewrite rows 1 and 3 to split ordinary and envelope modes. Row 1, ordinary mode: preflight or trace-generation failure, no JSON. Row 1, envelope mode: the envelope `status` is `failed`, including `guest_exception` and `guest_exit`, where `trace` can still hold captured snapshots, so inspect the envelope before stderr. Row 3: any `stopped` status, budget or not. Keep one normative copy of the exit-status table (the cli.md table is the most findable) and replace the prose at BOUNDED_TRACING.md:151-159 with a link to it, so the two copies cannot drift again.

evidence.detail: Ordinary and envelope CLI tracing both call TraceDispatch.dedicated().
Single-stack jobs use TraceDispatch.persistent(legacyGuest()). Multithread jobs close the session and use TraceDispatch.dedicated().
One-shot Tracer.trace runs through `new BatchTraceWorker(1)`, so it also uses a persistent guest for single-stack jobs.
The implementation calls --max-jobs-per-worker "Jobs before recycling a reusable guest". The help text calls the same thing a "worker process".

evidence.ref: printf jobs with System.exit(2), System.exit(0), then a normal job | java -jar target/code-tracer.jar batch-trace
evidence.detail: exit2: failed guest_exit, guestExitCode 2. exit0: failed guest_exit, guestExitCode 0. The following job completes. `trace -i Quit0.java --format modern --result-envelope` (System.exit(0)) exits 0 with status completed.
The ordinary CLI trace captures with TraceDispatch.dedicated().capture(...).
The envelope CLI (executeBoundedSource) sets phase("trace") and then calls TraceDispatch.dedicated().capture(...), so a dedicated launch happens inside the trace phase.

prepareGuest calls ensureSession() (PersistentGuestSession) for single-stack jobs and close() for multithread jobs. Dispatch is job.multithread() ? TraceDispatch.dedicated() : TraceDispatch.persistent(legacyGuest()).
One-shot Java uses try (BatchTraceWorker worker = new BatchTraceWorker(1)), so each Tracer.trace call starts and closes its own persistent guest for single-stack requests.

prepareGuest(job) runs before the TraceSession is created, and the deadline clock (started = System.nanoTime()) starts only at phase("trace"). Persistent-guest startup is therefore outside the timeout for both batch jobs and Tracer.trace.

findings.original_problem: Several result contracts depend on whether a job ran in a dedicated or a persistent guest: what the timeout covers (BOUNDED 17-19, 48), what `guest_exit` means (146), whether `guestExitCode` is reported, and which loader behaviour applies (java-api 236). The pages name the same two modes nine ways: dedicated guest, reusable guest, persistent guest (java-api 236; GLOSSARY 95; class PersistentGuestSession), reused guest (batch 57), reusable single-stack guest (output 193), batch daemon (batch 176), guest JVM, fresh JVM (batch 87-89), and the help's "worker process" and "worker sessions" (cli 121, 123). No page defines the terms or says that CLI `trace` always uses a dedicated guest while batch-trace and one-shot `Tracer.trace` use a persistent guest for single-stack jobs. A reader cannot tell which contract applies. For example, a program that calls System.exit(0) is `completed` through `trace --result-envelope` but `failed`/`guest_exit` through batch-trace and, by the same worker code path, Tracer.trace, and the docs give the reader no way to predict this.
findings.original_fix: Add a short reference section, for example in BOUNDED_TRACING.md or the user glossary proposed in a separate finding, that defines "dedicated guest" and "persistent (reusable) guest". Include a table mapping entry points to guest modes: CLI trace is always dedicated; batch-trace, BatchTracer and Tracer.trace are persistent for single-stack jobs and dedicated for multithread jobs. Use one term (persistent, matching the implementation and GLOSSARY) everywhere, and replace "batch daemon", "reused guest" and "worker process". State the per-entry-point consequences at timeout, guest_exit (including System.exit(0) in persistent guests) and guestExitCode, and link the stop-code row to the new section.

findings.title: Multi-file source format is a shared contract with six names and no reference definition
findings.quote: Required, nonblank Java source text, optionally a delimited multi-file bundle.
findings.problem: The CLI stdin and --input, batch `source`, `TraceRequest` source, `--max-source-files`/`sourceFiles` and the runner's input all depend on one multi-file text format. The pages call it six things: "delimited multi-file bundle" (batch 31), "delimiter-defined source files" (BOUNDED 58), "delimited stream" (BOUNDED 98), "Streamed source files" (CLI help), "existing delimited multi-file syntax" (java-api 115) and "source bundle" (RUNNER 42; GLOSSARY uses "Source bundle" for the Java SourceBundle value). No page defines the syntax. The only sources are one example (tracing.md) and the exact line SourceBundle emits (java-api 303). Integrators writing bundles by hand cannot learn the real rules: delimiter markers, path requirements, or how the entry file and source_file_limit counting work.

evidence.detail: A delimiter line is `//`, optional spaces or tabs, at least 3 `-` or `=` markers, a path ending in `.java`, then at least 3 markers. The accepted grammar is broader than the single documented spelling.

evidence.ref:
printf '//=== demo/Helper.java ===
...
//	------ demo/Main.java -----
...' | java -jar target/code-tracer.jar trace --format modern
evidence.detail: Both spellings are accepted as delimiters: sources are ['demo/Helper.java', 'demo/Main.java'], entryFile is demo/Main.java and stdout is '42\n'.

findings.fix: Add a "Multi-file source format" reference section, for example in output.md or a new docs/reference/source-format.md. It should define the delimiter grammar, path rules (relative, .java, no escape or duplicate destinations), handling of text before the first delimiter, entry-file selection, and how files are counted for sourceFiles. Use one name ("delimited source bundle") consistently and link to the section from batch.md `source`, the BOUNDED `--max-source-files` row, the CLI reference, java-api.md and RUNNER_CONTRACT.

findings.title: Single-thread stacks include JDK frames whose `file` is not in `sources`; the reference implies otherwise
findings.quote: Step and frame `file` values select the corresponding source; line numbers are 1-based. Discovered dependencies outside the submitted bundle are not included in `sources`.
findings.problem: The reference tells consumers that a frame's `file` selects its source. In single-thread capture, though, every suspended frame except harness and reflection frames is captured, including JDK library frames with their locals, such as Collections.sort and TimSort. Those frames' `file` values (for example 'java/util/Collections.java') are not keys in `sources`. Multithread capture keeps only submitted application frames (output.md:156), so the same program yields different stacks in the two modes, and the JDK frames listed vary between JDK 21 and 25. The trace-model explanation (trace-model.md:28-32) describes `callStack` as 'captured method frames' without saying which frames are captured. A visualizer that resolves each frame's source by key will hit missing entries, and students will see JDK frames they did not write.

evidence.detail: isCapturedClass returns true for every class when no ThreadCapture is active, so only harness and reflection frames are skipped. With multithread, only applicationClass names (ThreadCapture.java:137-139) are captured.

findings.title: Trust model is stated only as rules; no page explains what an unsandboxed guest can access
findings.quote: Capturing state also does not isolate guest execution. The program still runs; hosted untrusted submissions require the separate protections described in the [runner contract](../RUNNER_CONTRACT.md).
findings.problem: Readers get only a rule: run trusted programs locally and follow the runner contract for hosted submissions (README.md:30-33, index.md:26-27, first-trace.md:89-90, batch.md:95-98). RUNNER_CONTRACT.md lists runner requirements ('a minimal environment without secrets', line 18) but never states what a guest can reach by default. No page explains that the guest JVM is a child process running as the invoking user. It inherits that process's environment variables and working directory, and it can read and write files and use the network. This applies equally when an application calls Tracer.trace in-process. Relative file paths in guest code resolve against the tracer's working directory. Budgets, FIELDS, and class-loader separation do not restrict any of this. The docs also do not cover the middle case between 'trusted local' and 'hosted': an instructor tracing a student's submission on their own machine. That reader has no basis for judging the risk, and an embedder does not learn that the service's own secrets are exposed to the guest.

findings.title: TRUSTED vs FIELDS trade-off is buried in the limits page and never explained
findings.quote: `TRUSTED` retains existing specialized collection, map, wrapper, and stream inspection. It can invoke guest methods
findings.problem: Inspection policy changes what students see and whether the tracer runs guest code during capture. Its only explanation sits under 'Inspection policies' in a page titled 'Bounded tracing and result schema v1', and no page links that section. The trace-model explanation only mentions 'inspection policy' in passing (trace-model.md:62-63). Troubleshooting sends readers to a representation the docs never show: 'Check the requested inspection policy and compare its documented representation' (troubleshooting.md:46, no link). Nothing explains: TRUSTED presents collections and wrappers by their logical contents by calling guest methods, which can change the very execution being traced. FIELDS shows JDK-specific internals, so an ArrayList becomes an object with elementData, size, and modCount. The name TRUSTED means trusting the guest's methods, not a security tier. Choosing FIELDS also switches source discovery to submitted-only. The ordinary CLI refuses FIELDS without --result-envelope. Multithread capture forces FIELDS. Without this, instructors cannot predict how collections will look, and integrators cannot see why the runner contract recommends FIELDS.

findings.title: No page explains why two JSON formats exist or how to choose between pytutor and modern
findings.quote: The tracer supports Python Tutor (`pytutor`, default) and modern (`modern`) JSON.
findings.problem: Format is the first decision an integrator makes, and the docs give no basis for it. pytutor is the default for the CLI, batch, and the Java convenience request, yet every runnable tutorial and recipe uses `--format modern`. Only tracing.md:265 names pytutor, and only to say it is the default. batch.md:169 calls it 'legacy Python Tutor output', implying it is deprecated, but no page says so. No page says what 'Python Tutor-compatible' means: which renderer consumes it, or which Java-specific extensions (locals_attrs, heap_attrs, stdinConsumed, stderr) a stock Python Tutor frontend would ignore. No page says what each format cannot represent: pytutor cannot hold multithread capture, and its selected-breakpoint root is a dictionary of complete payloads. The explanation page describes the trace model only in modern terms (trace-model.md:30). Instructors who want Python Tutor output and integrators building new consumers cannot tell which format is recommended or what they give up.

findings.title: Trace model promises input observation but never explains it; meaning of stdinConsumed varies by reader
findings.quote: It connects source locations, active method calls, variable values, reachable objects, and observed input/output.
findings.problem: The explanation page says it connects observed input/output, but its only section covers output (lines 82-97). Input observation is described only in two reference sentences (output.md:77-82) that say it 'recognizes supported standard-input readers' without naming them. Behaviour differs by reader. For Scanner, BufferedReader.readLine, and IO.readln, stdinConsumed is a logical cursor: after nextLine it shows only the line read, even though Scanner has buffered more. For other readers built on System.in, such as InputStreamReader, it reflects the underlying stream's buffered reads: after the program reads 3 chars, it shows the whole input. Instructors who use stdinConsumed to show what a program has read cannot tell when it reflects the program's reads and when it reflects buffering.

findings.title: Runtime exception-recognition defect persists; Javadoc now documents it
findings.quote:
An exception escaping the student entry point produces `status: "failed"`,
`stopReason: "guest_exception"`, and `complete: false`, with the useful partial
trace retained. The harness prints the original exception message and stack trace
into the counted guest stderr stream before the job completion barrier.
findings.problem: Single-stack persistent execution can still report completed/complete=true for uncaught exceptions thrown in JDK/dependency code. Javadoc now warns explicitly, but implementation and Markdown reference/tutorial guidance are unchanged. Ordinary guest code can write stderr, so its contents are not a stable machine classifier.

findings.title: Single-stack modern format also emits event: "step_line" for terminal exception snapshots
findings.quote:
For legacy Python Tutor output, the terminal snapshot remains `step_line` at the
failing source location. It can immediately follow a pre-statement snapshot at
that same line.
findings.problem: Saying 'For legacy Python Tutor output, the terminal snapshot remains `step_line` at the failing source location' implies that `modern` format uses a different `event` value (such as `"exception"`, documented in `docs/reference/output.md` for thread capture) in single-stack jobs. In fact, `SnapshotCapture.capture()` sets `snapshot.event()` to `null` whenever `session.threadCapture()` is null (all single-stack jobs), and `ModernTraceSerializer.createStep()` serializes `null` as `"step_line"`. Thus single-stack `modern` traces also emit `event: "step_line"` for the terminal uncaught-exception snapshot.

evidence.detail: snapshot.event() is populated from session.threadCapture(), which is non-null only when multithread capture is enabled.
createStep() defaults step.event to "step_line" whenever snapshot.event() is null.
Produces modern steps with (line 3, event: "step_line"), (line 4, event: "step_line"), and terminal exception snapshot (line 4, event: "step_line").

findings.title: Unreadable --stdin-file throws before runBounded, emitting no JSON envelope on exit 1
findings.quote:
| `1` | Environment preflight or trace generation failed. | Read stderr. With an envelope, also inspect `status`, `phase`, and `diagnostics` if an envelope was produced. |
| `2` | Invalid command arguments or configuration. | Read stderr and compare the invocation with `trace --help`. |
| `3` | A tracing limit caused a controlled stop. | With `--result-envelope`, inspect the stopped result and any retained prefix. Ordinary mode emits a diagnostic without partial JSON. |

Preflight runs before command work and can prevent an envelope from being produced.
findings.problem: The exit-status table and note explain missing envelopes on exit status `1` only by pointing to JDK environment preflight (and `docs/BOUNDED_TRACING.md:155-158` states that in `trace --result-envelope`, exit `1` is for failed jobs while invalid CLI configuration uses exit `2` and need not produce an envelope). However, `App.Trace.run()` calls `resolveGuestStdin()` before `runBounded()` opens a `TraceSession`, inside a `try` block that catches only `IllegalArgumentException`. When `--stdin-file` names a missing, unreadable, or directory path, `Files.readString(stdinFile.toPath())` fails and `resolveGuestStdin()` throws an uncaught `RuntimeException("Failed to read stdin file: ...")`. Picocli catches that exception, prints a raw Java stack trace to `stderr` (even without `--verbose`), writes nothing to `stdout` (no JSON result envelope), and exits with status `1`—whereas a missing `--input` source file is read inside `runBounded()` (`readBoundedSource`) and produces a valid failed JSON envelope on `stdout` (`status: "failed"`, `stopReason: "compile_error"`, `phase: "source"`, empty `stderr`, exit `1`). Automated callers that expect `trace --result-envelope` to emit a JSON envelope for file-input failures after preflight succeeds will fail to parse empty `stdout` when `--stdin-file` cannot be read.

evidence.detail: `Trace.resolveGuestStdin()` wraps `IOException` from `Files.readString(stdinFile.toPath())` in `new RuntimeException("Failed to read stdin file: " + stdinFile, e)` (line 322), and `Trace.run()` calls `guestStdin = resolveGuestStdin()` (line 333) before `if (job.envelope) { runBounded(selected, guestStdin); return; }` (lines 342-345) in a `try` block that only catches `IllegalArgumentException` (line 347).

By contrast, `runBounded()` reads `--input` via `readBoundedSource(session, limits)` (lines 409, 444) inside `try (TraceSession session = ...)` and `catch (Exception caught)`, emitting a `TraceResult` JSON envelope with `phase: "source"` and `stopReason: "compile_error"` on `stdout` before exiting with status `1`.

Exits with status 1, leaves stdout completely empty (0 bytes), and prints `java.lang.RuntimeException: Failed to read stdin file: .../missing.txt` with a full stack trace to stderr; running `java -jar target/code-tracer.jar trace --result-envelope --input Missing.java` exits with status 1, leaves stderr empty, and emits `{"schemaVersion":1,"format":"pytutor","status":"failed","stopReason":"compile_error","phase":"source",...}` on stdout.

States `With trace --result-envelope, exit codes are 0 for completed jobs, 1 for failed jobs, 2 for invalid CLI configuration, and 3 for controlled stops. Invalid CLI configuration follows Picocli's stderr diagnostics and need not produce an envelope`, omitting that `--stdin-file` I/O failures also exit with status 1 without producing an envelope.

findings.fix: Document that --stdin-file read errors happen before envelope creation and can return exit 1 with empty stdout and stderr diagnostics. Explain how callers distinguish this from a structured failure envelope.

findings.title: Envelope phase on normal completion and source_file_limit differs between CLI and batch/Java
findings.quote:
- `phase`: usually `source`, `compile`, `trace`, or `serialize` at
  completion/failure. Batch request parsing can report `parse`; Java and batch
  configuration or guest-startup failures can report `validation` or `tracer`.
findings.problem: The envelope field description treats `phase` as uniform across envelope entry points (`trace --result-envelope`, `batch-trace`, and `Tracer.trace`), but CLI `trace --result-envelope` transitions `phase` differently from `batch-trace` and `Tracer.trace` in two places: (1) on normal completion (`status: "completed"`), `App.Trace.executeBoundedSource()` leaves the session in `phase: "trace"` and `TraceCompletion.envelope()` only sets `session.phase("serialize")` inside its `catch (RuntimeException)` handler when sequence rendering fails, so `trace --result-envelope` reports `"phase": "trace"` on every completed job, whereas `TraceCompletion.workerSuccess()` (used by `batch-trace` and `Tracer.trace`) calls `session.phase("serialize")` before rendering and reports `"phase": "serialize"` on every completed job; (2) when `--max-source-files` (`source_file_limit`) stops a job, `App.Trace.runBounded()` calls `session.phase("compile")` before enforcing `limits.sourceFiles()`, reporting `"phase": "compile"`, whereas `BatchTraceWorker.prepareSource()` enforces `limits.sourceFiles()` before `traceSession.phase("compile")`, reporting `"phase": "source"`. Integrators sharing envelope consumers across CLI and batch/Java modes will see contradictory `phase` values for identical jobs.

evidence.detail: `Trace.runBounded()` sets `session.phase("compile")` at line 411 before `session.enforce(Math.max(1, files), limits.sourceFiles(), "source_file_limit")` at line 413; `executeBoundedSource()` sets `session.phase("trace")` at line 473; and `TraceCompletion.envelope()` is called at line 424 without setting `phase` to `"serialize"` on success.

`TraceCompletion.envelope()` (lines 93-102) sets `session.phase("serialize")` only in `catch (RuntimeException serializationFailure)` (line 100), whereas `TraceCompletion.workerSuccess()` (lines 116-129) unconditionally calls `session.phase("serialize")` at lines 124 and 127 before `renderer.render(...)`.
`BatchTraceWorker.prepareSource()` enforces `source_limit` and `source_file_limit` (lines 194-196) while `phase` is still `"source"`, before calling `traceSession.phase("compile")` at line 198.

Emits `"status":"completed","stopReason":null,"phase":"trace"`, whereas running the same program through `batch-trace` emits `"status":"completed","stopReason":null,"phase":"serialize"`; similarly, `--max-source-files 1` on a 2-file bundle emits `"stopReason":"source_file_limit","phase":"compile"` in `trace --result-envelope` vs `"stopReason":"source_file_limit","phase":"source"` in `batch-trace`.

findings.title: CLI trace --result-envelope omits final-output projection onto earlier selected breakpoints
findings.quote:
Snapshot `stdout` and `stderr` contain cumulative captured output. Chronological
snapshots record progress; after execution, the final snapshot receives trailing
output when budgets permit. Selected-breakpoint presentation also refreshes the
latest retained hit at each location with final output. A result envelope carries
the available guest streams even when no usable snapshot payload exists.
findings.problem: The output reference states unconditionally that selected-breakpoint presentation refreshes the latest retained hit at each location with final guest output (and `GLOSSARY.md:101-109` states that **Trace completion** selects retained snapshots for both envelope CLI and Java/NDJSON worker payloads while **Snapshot retention** owns output projection). That contract holds for non-envelope CLI `trace --breakpoints ...`, `batch-trace`, and `Tracer.trace`, where `TraceCompletion.workerSuccess()` and `TraceCompletion.workerRecovery()` call `session.targetedSnapshots()` (`SnapshotRetention.targetedSnapshots()`) to copy the final `stdout`/`stderr` slices onto the latest retained snapshot at each `(sourcePath, line)`. In CLI `trace --result-envelope`, however, `App.Trace.executeBoundedSource()` calls `session.finishOutput()`—which updates only `completed.getLast()`, the single final snapshot overall—and returns `session.snapshots()` instead of `session.targetedSnapshots()` (and `TraceCompletion.envelope()` likewise falls back to `session.snapshots()`). Consequently, for any multi-location selected-breakpoint run under `trace --result-envelope` (such as `--result-envelope --breakpoints 4,6`, with or without `--accumulate-breakpoints`), only the last overall snapshot receives trailing `stdout`/`stderr`, while the latest retained hits at all earlier breakpoint locations retain only the partial output captured when those lines executed.

evidence.detail: `Trace.executeBoundedSource()` runs `TraceDispatch.dedicated().capture(...)`, calls `session.finishOutput()`, and returns `session.snapshots()` instead of `session.targetedSnapshots()`.

`TraceCompletion.workerSuccess()` and `workerRecovery()` select snapshots via `retainedSnapshots(job, session)`, which returns `job.capture().chronological() ? session.snapshots() : session.targetedSnapshots()`, whereas `TraceCompletion.envelope()` uses the caller-supplied `session.snapshots()` list (or `session.snapshots()` on recovery at line 96) without calling `session.targetedSnapshots()`.

`SnapshotRetention.finishOutput()` (lines 186-215) updates only `completed.getLast()` with the final `stdout` and `stderr` slices; projecting that final output onto the latest hit at each earlier `(sourcePath, line)` requires `SnapshotRetention.targetedSnapshots()` (lines 84-99).

For a `Main.java` that prints `from-4:1
` on line 4 and `from-6:2
` on line 6, `trace --result-envelope --format modern --breakpoints 4,6` produces `steps[0].stdout == ""` at line 4 and `steps[1].stdout == "from-4:1
from-6:2
"` at line 6, whereas `batch-trace` with `"format":"modern","breakpoints":[4,6]` produces `"from-4:1
from-6:2
"` on both `steps[0]` and `steps[1]`.

Defines **Snapshot retention** as owning output projection and **Trace completion** as selecting completed or retained snapshots for both envelope CLI and Java/NDJSON worker result payloads under the caller's completion rules, without noting that envelope CLI skips targeted-breakpoint output projection.

findings.fix: Qualify the selected-breakpoint final-output rule for CLI --result-envelope and contrast it with ordinary CLI and Java/batch projection. A Java behavior change is a separate task.

findings.title: Java guide omits runtime prerequisites now documented in Javadoc
findings.quote:
Run with a full **JDK 21 or later**; CI exercises Java 21 and 25, and `.java-version`
selects the local development JDK.
findings.problem: Tracer Javadoc now identifies modules, subprocess permissions and directly filesystem-addressable implementation requirements. Markdown still names only a full JDK and runtime dependencies. Packaging support and runtime behavior did not change.

evidence.detail: Objects.requireNonNull(ToolProvider.getSystemJavaCompiler(), "System Java compiler unavailable (run on a JDK, not a JRE)").
Uses Bootstrap.virtualMachineManager().defaultConnector() (JDI LaunchingConnector) and resolves GuestSystemClassLoader's CodeSource URL via Path.of(location.toURI()) for the child JVM's -classpath.
Path harnessCp = Path.of(GuestHarness.class.getProtectionDomain().getCodeSource().getLocation().toURI()); VirtualMachine vm = GuestLauncher.launch(GuestHarness.class.getName(), harnessCp, true);

findings.fix: Add these host/runtime/packaging requirements and Tracer Javadoc links to existing Java Markdown, retaining the synthetic-test qualification.

original_evidence.detail: Objects.requireNonNull(ToolProvider.getSystemJavaCompiler(), "System Java compiler unavailable (run on a JDK, not a JRE)").
Uses Bootstrap.virtualMachineManager().defaultConnector() (JDI LaunchingConnector) and resolves GuestSystemClassLoader's CodeSource URL via Path.of(location.toURI()) for the child JVM's -classpath.
Path harnessCp = Path.of(GuestHarness.class.getProtectionDomain().getCodeSource().getLocation().toURI()); VirtualMachine vm = GuestLauncher.launch(GuestHarness.class.getName(), harnessCp, true);

findings.original_problem:
`docs/reference/java-api.md` tells library embedders to 'Use the regular tracer JAR for library integration and supply its Maven runtime dependencies' and 'Run with a full JDK 21 or later', and notes that `Tracer.trace` 'uses the same job execution implementation as batch tracing and closes its worker before returning', without documenting the operational and packaging requirements that `Tracer.trace`, `Tracer.discoverBreakpoints`, and `BatchTracer` impose on the host JVM:
1. In-process compilation requires `javax.tools.ToolProvider.getSystemJavaCompiler()` (`jdk.compiler` module).
2. Every `Tracer.trace` call and `BatchTracer` worker spawns a child JVM subprocess via JDI's default `LaunchingConnector` (`com.sun.jdi.Bootstrap.virtualMachineManager().defaultConnector()`, requiring `jdk.jdi` and an executable `java` launcher under the host JVM's `java.home`).
3. Both `PersistentGuestSession.start()` and `GuestLauncher.launch()` resolve the filesystem path of `GuestHarness.class` / `GuestSystemClassLoader.class` via `Path.of(getProtectionDomain().getCodeSource().getLocation().toURI())` and pass it as a `-classpath` file path to the child JVM. If an embedder packages the library inside a nested fat-JAR (`jar:file:...!/BOOT-INF/lib/...`, such as a Spring Boot executable archive) or loads it from a non-`file:` `CodeSource` URI, guest launch fails with `FileSystemNotFoundException` or `IOException("Invalid guest loader location")` (surfacing as `status: "failed"`, `phase: "tracer"` or `"trace"`, `stopReason: "tracer_error"`).
findings.original_fix: Add a brief host-runtime and packaging subsection or paragraph in `docs/reference/java-api.md` stating that `Tracer.discoverBreakpoints` requires `jdk.compiler` (`ToolProvider.getSystemJavaCompiler()`), `Tracer.trace` and `BatchTracer` additionally require `jdk.jdi` (`LaunchingConnector`) and spawn child guest JVM processes using the host `java.home`, and the tracer JAR must reside at a direct filesystem (`file:`) code-source path rather than nested inside an unpacked archive (such as a `BOOT-INF/lib` nested JAR).

adjudications.rationale: Code inspection confirms ToolProvider.getSystemJavaCompiler for source compilation; JDI default LaunchingConnector for child JVMs; and Path.of(GuestHarness CodeSource URI) for persistent guest startup. Runtime probe confirms compiler module jdk.compiler, Bootstrap module jdk.jdi, and connector default home equal to active java.home. A synthetic classloader that assigns GuestHarness a jar:file:...!/BOOT-INF/lib/tracer.jar CodeSource makes the public API return failed/tracer_error/phase tracer with null trace. Full-JDK and regular-JAR requirements are already stated, so document practical subprocess/direct-filesystem packaging implications without presenting module names as new requirements for standard full JDK users. Actual Spring Boot, custom jlink images, and alternate vendor JDKs were not exercised.

votes.reason: `docs/reference/java-api.md` already instructs embedders to 'Run with a full JDK 21 or later' and 'Use the regular tracer JAR for library integration and supply its Maven runtime dependencies,' which works in standard Maven/classpath deployments (`category` is `missing-topic`). However, omitting the concrete host runtime and packaging constraints—specifically that `Tracer.trace` and `BatchTracer` require `jdk.compiler` and `jdk.jdi`, spawn child guest JVMs via `java.home`, and require `cs1302-tracer` to reside at a filesystem (`file:`) `CodeSource` path rather than inside a nested fat-JAR (`BOOT-INF/lib`)—leaves an important operational contract for library embedders undocumented (`S3`).

In scope: documents host JVM module (`jdk.compiler`, `jdk.jdi`), child-process launch (`java.home`), and filesystem `file:` `CodeSource` requirements for library embedders in `docs/reference/java-api.md`. Preserves URLs, requires no Java code changes, and is not already covered on `docs/reference/java-api.md` or its linked sections.

findings.title: Nesting stop codes omit phase and droppedSnapshots distinction between pre-run and capture checks
findings.quote:
The tracer also enforces fixed nesting limits of `32` for inline `TraceValue`
trees and `64` for batch JSON request depth, and rejects cyclic inline

adjudications.rationale: The fixed nesting codes and safety checks are real. A legal 70-level nested generic declaration reproduces stopped/type_nesting_limit/phase trace/droppedSnapshots=0 before any retained snapshots in both CLI and batch. Current code sets extracting=true in beginSnapshot and clears it only after successful retention, while result copies extracting into droppedSnapshots; ValueTraversal validates both retention and serializer entry. These facts support the phase/drop distinction, but an externally reachable serializer-only or inline-cycle request was not constructed, and snapshots are internal structures with a documented no-mutation rule. The raw report also uses stale implementation names ValueNesting/afterSnapshot/substituteTypeParams, now ValueTraversal/commit/substituteType. Existing nesting-boundaries explanation plus F30-4 already covers code consolidation. Do not create another standalone finding; include concise distinctions only where needed in that table.
